title: Six Ways to Make People Like You
coreMove: Spend your attention on what makes the other person feel important — their name, their interests, their own talk — before you offer a single thing about yourself.

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospice nurse arriving for her first visit with a man who has stopped speaking to most visitors
exampleSpecs.audience: a hospice nurse three months into her first hospice rotation
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she gets the patient to say a single full sentence today, which his daughter has begged for
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she opens by asking about the framed photograph on his dresser, not about how he is feeling, and he begins to talk about the river in the picture

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school basketball coach trying to reach a transfer player who will not make eye contact at practice
exampleSpecs.audience: a coach in the second week of a new season
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the player stays on the roster or quits by Friday and tells his friends the program is cold
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coach asks about the player's old gym, listens for three full minutes without correcting anything, and only then mentions tomorrow's drill

exampleSpecs.domain: a tax preparer sitting with a recently widowed woman who keeps apologizing for asking the same question twice
exampleSpecs.audience: a small-practice tax preparer who is already running thirty minutes late on the day
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the client trusts him enough to come back next April, when her return becomes genuinely complicated
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he repeats her late husband's first name back to her gently when she mentions it, and uses that same name again twenty minutes later as if he had known the man

exampleSpecs.domain: a head line cook newly promoted to expediter who decides to learn the name of every server who comes to the pass
exampleSpecs.audience: a line cook in his first month running tickets
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the front of house begins to trust the kitchen instead of grumbling at it through the next Saturday rush
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: on the busiest service of the month he calls each server by name as their plates leave the window, and the floor returns less food, not because cooking changed but because mood did

exampleSpecs.domain: a dental hygienist treating a sixteen-year-old who has shown up in earbuds and refuses small talk
exampleSpecs.audience: a hygienist who has already tried weather and weekend plans and gotten nothing back
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the teenager will actually start flossing instead of lying about flossing for another six months
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she notices the band logo on his hoodie and asks one specific question about the drummer in that band, and he pulls out an earbud to answer

exampleSpecs.domain: a hotel night auditor on the front desk at 2 a.m. when a stranded business traveler walks in furious about a missed shuttle
exampleSpecs.audience: a night auditor who has been told by her manager that she is too quiet to handle complaints
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the guest writes a one-star review or asks for her by name on his next trip through the city
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she does not defend the hotel; she asks his name, uses it twice, and asks where he was supposed to be tonight, and the anger drains out of him before she has typed anything

exampleSpecs.domain: a parent volunteering at a fourth-grade book fair who notices a boy nobody is standing near
exampleSpecs.audience: a parent who has always felt awkward around children who are not her own
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether one quiet afternoon becomes a small lift this boy will remember the next time he feels invisible
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she does not ask his grade or his favorite subject; she asks which book he picked up first and why, and he tells her at length while she does not interrupt once
